headline: High: shared-note retrieval plus broad egress creates leakage and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection is lower because no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented shared channel to Khoj, and Khoj’s documented bridges are files and APIs rather than direct ingestion of Botpress outputs. However, Khoj can read indexed files and Botpress is an LLM chatbot, so manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry instructions. The pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Botpress output into a Khoj-indexed note or file, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF Khoj is configured to ingest Botpress-generated content from shared files, then attacker instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Khoj in separate workspaces.
Disable automatic indexing of Botpress transcripts in Khoj.
Use a human review step before copying Botpress output into Khoj.
Tag Botpress-generated content as untrusted in notes.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress, while Botpress has no network egress. If Botpress output is stored in Khoj’s indexed workspace, sensitive note content can be surfaced into Botpress conversations or downstream APIs. The pair does not prove exfiltration, but the shared-document pathway exists in default-style use.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are written into files that Khoj indexes, then those contents can be retrieved in later chats.
IF Khoj is connected to external search providers, then retrieved note content can leave the local workspace.
mitigations: Exclude sensitive folders from Khoj indexing.
Store Botpress transcripts outside Khoj’s indexed paths.
Turn off external search providers for sensitive sessions.
Review retrieved snippets before sending them to users.
requires-engineering: enforce per-source access controls on indexed documents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it or modify git state. That means the pair has limited overlapping mutation risk: Botpress may change its own environment, but Khoj lacks the write primitives needed for direct conflict. The interaction is mostly read-only from Khoj’s side.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through an external orchestrator, then conflict risk increases.
IF an operator grants Khoj write access outside the documented profile, then overlapping writes become possible.
mitigations: Keep Khoj read-only on shared directories.
Run Botpress in an isolated environment.
Avoid pointing both agents at the same git checkout.
Monitor package installs from Botpress.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around any shared workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj’s retrieval-and-chat flow can treat indexed content as authoritative, and Botpress is a conversational generator that may emit unverified facts. If Botpress output is indexed or pasted into Khoj, Khoj can propagate those errors into later answers. No verification step is documented in the pair, so the cascade is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated text is indexed by Khoj, then later Khoj answers may reuse its errors.
IF Khoj is used to draft user-facing responses without manual verification, then incorrect Botpress content can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of Botpress outputs before indexing.
Mark Botpress content as untrusted in Khoj prompts.
Use citations or source links for retrieved claims.
Separate drafting and retrieval workflows.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before Khoj can reuse external text.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. If personal or regulated data from Khoj flows into Botpress, the pair creates a compliance mismatch risk. The evidence is docs-only, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF personal notes from Khoj are copied into Botpress conversations, then retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF regulated data is present in Khoj’s indexed documents, then Botpress handling must match that regime.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Botpress chats.
Document retention rules for both systems.
Restrict Botpress to non-sensitive support content.
Review data-processing terms before connecting the pair.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
